distr continuous, whole real line¶

Families whose values range over the whole real line: the normal and its heavy-tailed and skewed relatives, and the mixtures built from them. Each page documents one family: the parameters, the support, how to evaluate the density and the distribution function, how to draw samples, and, for the families that have one, the object form and the maximum-likelihood fit.

The Surface¶

Family

What it is

Cauchy

The Cauchy distribution: a symmetric bell-shaped curve with tails so heavy that it has no mean and no variance.

ExtremeValue

The extreme value (Gumbel) distribution: the distribution of the largest of many independent observations of a variable with an exponential-type tail.

Gh

The generalised hyperbolic distribution: a five-parameter family that contains the normal inverse Gaussian, the hyperbolic, the variance-gamma and, in a limit, the Student t.

HyperbolicSecant

The hyperbolic secant distribution: a symmetric density proportional to the hyperbolic secant, between the normal and the logistic in tail weight.

Laplace

The Laplace (double-exponential) distribution: a symmetric peak with exponentially decaying tails, the distribution of the error whose best estimate is the median.

Logistic

The logistic distribution: a bell-shaped curve slightly heavier-tailed than the normal, whose distribution function is the logistic (sigmoid) function.

Nig

The normal inverse Gaussian distribution: a four-parameter family for skewed, heavy-tailed data.

Normal

The normal (Gaussian) distribution: the bell curve, determined by its mean and standard deviation.

StudentT

The Student t distribution: a bell-shaped curve with heavier tails than the normal, controlled by its degrees of freedom.

TukeyLambda

The Tukey lambda distribution: a one-parameter family defined through its quantile function that contains the logistic, uniform and approximately the normal and heavy-tailed distributions.
